Choosing which signals to transfer depends on student capacity and task; representation-level supervision often helps when student capacity permits, while logits are a low-cost, broadly useful signal (Anderson, 2022; Fisher, 2023).

Combining KD with other compression primitives: Practical systems combine KD with pruning, quantization, layer skipping, or architecture-aware optimization to jointly satisfy accuracy and resource budgets. Joint optimization frameworks that include a distillation loss can produce favorable FLOP/accuracy trade-offs in vision transformers and other architectures (Haynes, 2024; Fisher, 2023; Farmer, 2020).

Data regimes and sample-efficiency: KD can operate in full-data, low-data, and data-free regimes; success in low-data settings typically requires careful data augmentation, synthetic-data strategies, or pretraining of the student (Perkins summarized across works; see also Cortez, 2023). KD is often more sample-efficient than training from scratch but remains conditional on access to useful inputs or surrogates and on managing distribution shift (Anderson, 2022; Cortez, 2023).

Teacher quality, capacity mismatch, and failure modes: KD transfers teacher behavior and thus may propagate teacher errors or biases; capacity mismatch can prevent students from capturing teacher behaviors, especially for rare tokens or low-frequency phenomena. Empirically, distillation can diminish low-frequency lexical choices in certain sequence models, and exposing raw data or adjusting the objective can help mitigate such propagation (Robinson, 2019). Practitioners should evaluate distilled students on robustness, rare-event performance, and fairness metrics (Valdez, 2022; Tran, 2019).

Improving the transfer process: Several methodological extensions improve distillation outcomes: multi-teacher weighting or dynamic teacher selection, meta-learning to make teachers produce more transferable signals, and instance-aware weighting. Meta-learning frameworks where the teacher adapts to student feedback have shown robust improvements across student capacities (Walker, 2022; Bernard-style multi-teacher methods summarized in Fisher, 2023).

Applications and empirical evidence: KD has been effective across modalities and tasks: compressing large language and multimodal models, enabling multimodal generation by augmenting dual-stream models with textual PLMs via vision-language KD, and producing efficient 3D detectors with tailored distillation pipelines (Liu, 2020; Farmer, 2020). Empirical syntheses report consistent accuracy/efficiency gains when KD is integrated into a broader, task-aware pipeline (Anderson, 2022; Cortez, 2023).

Practical recommendations: Treat KD as a configurable component of compression pipelines: design the student architecture and pretraining schedule with the distillation recipe in mind; select distilled signals according to student capacity and task; use representation-level supervision where feasible; and combine KD with pruning/quantization to meet deployment budgets. Explicitly test for teacher error propagation and low-frequency or robustness degradations (Tran, 2019; Cortez, 2023; Valdez, 2022).

Open problems: Key unresolved issues include principled objective design that predicts which signals transfer best for a given teacher–student pair, reliable preservation of robustness and rare-event behavior under distillation, efficient distillation in severely data-limited or privacy-constrained settings, and theoretical understanding of when and why distillation improves generalization (Anderson, 2022; Fisher, 2023; Haynes, 2024).

Conclusion: Across vision, speech, and NLP, KD functions as the central, multifaceted tool for producing compact models when used in a task- and deployment-aware manner. Integrating KD with complementary compression techniques and with methods that address teacher imperfection and data limitations yields the best practical trade-offs, but addressing the remaining empirical and theoretical gaps is essential for reliably deploying distilled models in safety- or accuracy-critical settings (Tran, 2019; Valdez, 2022; Cortez, 2023).
